resources.string: Not sent: a message is at most %1$d bytes. Open Tern to write it shorter.
The node did not answer, so this may not have gone: %1$s. Open Tern to send it again.
Not sent: the node is not connected. Open Tern to write it again.
Pairing: enter the PIN your node shows, or 123456 if it has no screen. A node with no screen pairs only within 3 minutes of being turned on or its button pressed.
That device is not a Tern node, or its firmware is too old.
The phone and node could not agree a large enough packet size (MTU).

Pairing failed. If the node shows a passkey on its screen, type that one. If not, it pairs only for 3 minutes after someone is at it: press the node\'s button, or turn it off and on (press RESET on a board with no button), then pair within 3 minutes. If the node was reset or erased, remove it from Android\'s Bluetooth settings first.
The link dropped. Waiting for the node to come back.
the node\'s firmware does not know this request
not a valid address, or it is the node\'s own
the node has no room for another
the node had taken the app for gone
the Bluetooth packet size (MTU) is too small
the node is busy; try again shortly
the node is not in that group, or no longer holds that invite
the node is not where the update is
that is not firmware this node runs, or not signed by a key it trusts
that is not one of the node\'s contacts
that can\'t be done over the mesh
the node\'s Bluetooth is locked. Only USB, or one of its owners over the mesh, can unlock it
you\'re not one of the node\'s owners
your node asked who\'s about less than ten minutes ago. Try again in a few minutes
Your node\'s firmware does not support this yet.
The node did not answer. It may have done it anyway.
No Tern nodes found yet. Make sure yours is on and nearby.
Android asks for a PIN the first time. A node with a screen shows it; one without uses 123456 unless you changed it.
Tern needs Bluetooth permission to find and talk to your node.
If Android no longer asks, give Tern the permission in its settings.
On this version of Android, finding Bluetooth devices needs the phone\'s location setting on. Tern does not use your location.
Turn it on so Tern can find your node and talk to it.

plurals.name: connect_found
plurals.item: %1$d Tern node found nearby. Tap it to connect.
%1$d Tern nodes found nearby. Tap one to connect.

resources.string: Connect to a different node, or this one again
Tern stays off the node until you connect. Messages wait for you on the node.
The node stops sending and receiving, for you and everyone who relies on it. Tern cannot turn it on again: only its button, its reset or its power can, at the node itself.
The node restarted into its bootloader, which takes the new firmware over Bluetooth. It is off the air until it is done. Keep the phone near it.
The node is off. Turn it on at the node, with its button, its reset or its power, then connect.

The node erases everything it holds and starts again as a new node. Its address goes for good: contacts who know it can no longer reach it, and they must add its new one. Its contacts, groups and messages go for good too, from the node and from this app, and so do its settings and passkey. You will have to pair with it again. This cannot be undone.
The node starts again as a new one, with a new address. Tern forgot it, and this phone\'s Bluetooth pairing with it. To use it again, connect to it as a new node.
The node starts again as a new one, with a new address. Tern forgot it. Remove it from Android\'s Bluetooth settings too, before you pair with it again.
Tern disconnects and deletes the messages and contacts it saved from this node. They stay on the node, and come back if you connect to it again.
No conversations yet. Start one from a contact, or make a group.
That is your own node\'s address.
The node did not confirm this.
Still sending the same message. Send it again once the node answers.
Your node forgets the group\'s secret, and stops sharing your location with it. Its messages stay here. To be in it again, you need an invite or its join code from a member.
Anyone who sees this code, or is sent it, can join %1$s and read every message in it, from before as well as after. It can\'t be taken back, so show it only to people you would invite.
Scan this with Tern to join %1$s. Anyone who has this code can read the group.
Scan a group\'s join code, or paste its link. Only join a group from someone you trust.
The group has no name. You can name it once you have joined.
Not a join code, or one that was copied wrong.
That code is not a Tern join code.
Your node\'s firmware is too old to join a group from a join code. Update it from the Node tab, then open the link again.
The next message will set up a new session, with fresh keys.
Every message and invite in this chat is erased from your node, and from every phone or computer connected to it. This can\'t be undone. The contact and any secure session with them are kept.
Every message in this group\'s chat is erased from your node, and from every phone or computer connected to it. This can\'t be undone. You stay in the group.
Messages not yet delivered won\'t be sent.
Also delete your chat with them
No contacts yet. Add one by scanning the code on their Node tab, or from their link or address.
That is not a Tern link or address.
Point the camera at the code on a Tern node or app
That code does not hold a Tern address.
Check with the owner that their node shows this short code: %1$s
Someone else can scan this to add the same node.
They call themselves “%1$s”. The name you give is yours, and only you see it.

Your node forgets the name, stops sharing your location with this contact and forgets theirs. Your messages and any secure session with them are kept, but once that ends your node may turn away a new one they start.
Your node turned away a message from %1$s because it is not a contact.
Your node turned away a message from %1$s because it has no room for another session.
Their presence card says they are “%1$s”.
They say they are “%1$s”. That is only what they call themselves: check their short code with them before you save them.
No one about yet. Other people\'s nodes show up here when they turn their presence cards on and your node hears one. A card stays here for a day after it was last heard.
Each name is what that node says it is: anyone can put any name on a card. Before you trust one, check its short code with its owner.

This node\'s card says it is “%1$s”, which is only what its owner chose to call it. Check with them that their node shows this short code. Your node lets a contact reach you; adding one sends nothing.
This node\'s card carries no name. Check with its owner that their node shows this short code. Your node lets a contact reach you; adding one sends nothing.
Show my card to nodes nearby
On: your node sends its card
Off: your node sends no card

On, your node sends its address and the name above to every node in range, about every two hours, so anyone nearby can recognise it each time, and add it as a contact. Off, it puts neither on the air. Either way it shows you the cards of others.
The name on your card: the one name your node puts on the air, in clear, while its card is on. Empty for none.
Only this phone shows this name. It is not sent to your node, and no one else sees it. Leave it empty to use the Bluetooth name again.
Another Tern app scans this to add your node as a contact. A phone without Tern opens a page on ternmesh.org that shows the address.
Read this out to someone adding you: the code their phone shows should be the same.
No presence card heard from this node, so it has no name to show.
Relay: also passes on messages for others
Send at the most it may
6 digits, or empty for the node\'s default
Shown on the node\'s screen, new each time
This node still pairs with the default PIN, 123456.

This node has no screen, so it pairs with the default PIN, 123456. Until you choose your own, anyone nearby who knows the default can connect to it, read its messages and change its settings. This phone stays paired; you will need the new PIN to pair another.
No release number (built by hand), for %1$s
This node cannot be updated over Bluetooth. Flash it once over USB, at ternmesh.org/flash, and later updates can come this way.
Your node\'s firmware is too old to be updated over Bluetooth. Flash it once over USB, at ternmesh.org/flash, and later updates can come this way.
Could not reach ternmesh.org. Check the phone\'s internet connection and try again.
Up to date: %1$s is the latest release.
Release %1$s is published. Your node\'s firmware has no release number, so Tern cannot tell whether it is newer.
Release %1$s has no firmware for %2$s in %3$s.
Set the node\'s region first: its firmware is built for one.

Tern downloads the firmware, checks it, and sends it to the node over Bluetooth, which takes a few minutes. The node then restarts, and is off the air for a moment. Keep the phone near the node until it is done. Its messages, contacts and settings stay.
Waiting for the node to come back, to go on with the update…
The node is restarting into the new firmware…
The node did not confirm the last step. Waiting for it to come back, to see which firmware it runs…
The node did not start %1$s, and went back to %2$s.
The node still runs %2$s: the update to %1$s did not finish. Try again.
This node cannot be updated over Bluetooth. Flash it once over USB, at ternmesh.org/flash.
The node refused the update: this firmware is not signed by a key the node trusts, so nothing was sent. Its firmware is unchanged.

Release %1$s was published before Tern\'s releases were signed, and your node takes only signed firmware over Bluetooth, so it cannot be installed from here. Flash it over USB at ternmesh.org/flash, or wait for the next release.
This firmware is not signed, and your node takes only signed firmware over Bluetooth. Flash it over USB at ternmesh.org/flash.

Release %1$s carries no signature, so Tern cannot tell that it is the firmware the Tern project published: anyone who could change the download could have changed it. Releases from before signing began have none. Install it only if you trust where it came from.
Release %1$s is signed, but not by a key this app knows. It may not be the firmware the Tern project published, or this app may need updating first. Install it only if you trust where it came from.
Until the update finishes, anyone in Bluetooth range could give the node\'s bootloader firmware of their own: it checks no signature. Stay near the node and let it finish.
That is not firmware this node runs, so the node discarded it.
Could not download the firmware. Check the phone\'s internet connection and try again.
The node has changed since the check. Check for an update again.
The firmware downloaded is not the one published: it was not sent to the node. Try again.
Your node\'s firmware cannot take updates over Bluetooth.
Updating the node\'s firmware through its bootloader…
Updating the node\'s firmware: erasing the old one…
This node\'s bootloader cannot take firmware over Bluetooth. Update it over USB, at ternmesh.org/flash.

Tern downloads the firmware and checks it. The node then restarts into its bootloader, which takes the firmware over Bluetooth: about 5 minutes, while the node is off the air. Keep the phone near the node until it is done. If it stops part of the way, the node waits in its bootloader and trying again finishes it. Its messages, contacts and settings stay.
Asking the node to restart into its bootloader…
The node is restarting into its bootloader. Looking for it…
The bootloader is erasing the old firmware. This takes up to a minute or two. Keep the phone near the node.
Sending %1$s to the bootloader: %2$d%% (%3$s of %4$s). This takes about 5 minutes: keep the phone near the node.
The bootloader is checking the firmware…

Tern could not find the node\'s bootloader. If the node restarted into it, it is waiting there for the firmware: keep the phone near it and try again. If it did not, connect to the node. Its messages, contacts and settings are safe either way.

Tern found the node\'s bootloader but could not connect to it. The node is waiting in its bootloader for the firmware: keep the phone near it and try again. Its messages, contacts and settings are safe.
The update stopped part of the way: %1$s. The node is waiting in its bootloader for the firmware, and trying again will finish it. Its messages, contacts and settings are safe.
Your node does not transmit until it knows which radio rules to follow. Choose the region you are in.
Europe, the UK, Ukraine and South Africa
Thailand: the node raises its power to 17 dBm radiated if it is lower
The United States, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina and Peru
Only use a region that is legal where you are. You can change it later on the Node tab.
A relay passes on messages for nodes it can hear, which helps the mesh reach further but uses more battery. You can change this later.
Sends and receives its own messages only. Best for a node you carry.
Also passes on messages for others. Best for a node left somewhere high, on power.
Your node only accepts messages from contacts. Have a friend scan your code, and scan theirs: each of you adds the other.
Your node\'s firmware does not share positions. Update it from the Node tab.
No one is sharing their location with you yet.
On, the node works out where it is from satellites, on its own. Off saves its battery: it keeps the last position it had, and takes a newer one from your phone while you share your location.
Your node rounds your location to the size you pick before it leaves. The exact location stays between this phone and your node.
Without location access, your node shares only what its own receiver finds, if it has one.

Your node hears these, but they haven\'t shared a card, so all it knows is a short id, not who they are. To talk to one, ask its owner for their link or QR code, or wait for their card: nodes showing a card send one about every two hours.
Your node hears these, but all it knows of each is a short id, not who they are. To talk to one, ask its owner for their link or QR code.

Your node hears this one, but it hasn\'t shared a card, so all your node knows is its short id, not whose it is. You can\'t message or add it from here. To talk to it, ask its owner for their link or QR code, or wait for its card: nodes showing a card send one about every two hours.
Your node hears this one, but all it knows is its short id, not whose it is. You can\'t message or add it from here. To talk to it, ask its owner for their link or QR code.

Asks the nodes in range to send their cards now, instead of waiting up to two hours for the next. Only nodes within earshot hear it, and it carries nothing of yours. Your node can ask once every ten minutes.
Asked. Cards from nodes about arrive within half a minute.
Bars show how clearly your node hears each one: four is strong, one is at the edge of range. The number is the signal-to-noise ratio in dB.
Nothing heard from your node in this time. The app keeps what your node tells it while they\'re connected.
Your node\'s battery over the last %1$s
Your node tells the app its battery when it changes. The app keeps what it hears while connected, for a week, on this phone only: a gap in the line is a time it wasn\'t connected.
How much of its airtime limit your node used over the last %1$s

The radio rules in your node\'s region limit how long it may spend sending in each period. Airtime is how much of that it has used in the period just gone: when it runs out, messages wait until some frees up.
The app keeps what your node tells it while connected, for a week, on this phone only: a gap in the line is a time it wasn\'t connected.
Choose the region you are in
Use the region you are in. It sets the frequencies your node uses and how long it may transmit.
Sends and receives your own messages, and uses the least battery. Best for a node you carry.
Also passes on other people\'s messages, so the mesh reaches further. Best for a node left on a hill, at a hut or in a window.

Asleep, the node turns its radio off and wakes now and then to ask a nearby relay for what came for it. That saves its battery, but messages to it wait until it wakes. Its link to this phone stays on.
Relays never sleep: other nodes count on them. This setting applies when the node is a leaf.
It will check for messages every %1$s to start with. Messages to it wait with a nearby relay until it does, so they can take that long to arrive.
Waiting for a relay to keep its messages
No relay answers; trying %1$s again in %2$s
A relay: it does not sleep
Your node may restart to apply a change. The app connects again on its own.
A new PIN takes effect the next time a phone pairs. This phone stays paired.
%1$s was made an owner of %2$s, at the node.
%1$s was made an owner of %2$s, over the mesh.
%1$s is no longer an owner of %2$s, at the node.
%1$s is no longer an owner of %2$s, over the mesh.
If you didn\'t expect this, check who owns it.
Make %1$s an owner of your node?
An owner can change your node\'s settings, choose who it takes and restart it, from anywhere on the mesh. Only make an owner of a node you trust. Your node can have %1$d owners at most.
Requests go to %1$s over the mesh, one at a time. Tern shows what each is waiting for.
Waiting for %1$s. It may be asleep.
You\'re an owner of %1$s. Tap to manage it.
%1$s is asleep: it wakes every %2$d min, so this can take up to %2$d min.
The node restarts to apply it. Confirming once it can answer.
No answer. %1$s may be asleep or out of reach, or you\'re not an owner.
You\'re not an owner of %1$s. Its owner can add you.
Tern asks %1$s once, over the mesh. It answers only its owners.
Not yours: its owner can add you.
Asleep, it turns its radio off and wakes now and then to ask a nearby relay for what came for it, requests from you included. So while it sleeps, each answer can take as long as it sleeps.
A change made over the mesh is on trial for 15 minutes: the node goes back to how it was unless it hears from you again. Tern confirms it for you. Region and passkey can only be changed at the node.
Not confirmed. If the change put the node out of reach, it goes back by itself within 15 minutes.
Over Bluetooth it answers only a hello
Anyone who pairs with it can change it
Over Bluetooth it will answer nothing but a hello. Only USB, or one of its owners over the mesh, can unlock it.
An owner can manage the node from anywhere on the mesh. Any of its contacts can be one, up to %1$d. Every owner is told when this changes.
An owner can change its settings, choose who it takes and restart it, from anywhere on the mesh.
Your node will no longer be one of its owners, and can\'t manage it again unless someone at the node, or another owner, makes it one.
It stops for a few seconds and starts again. It keeps its settings, contacts and owners.
Over Bluetooth the node answers nothing but a hello, so this phone can see it but not change it. Unlock it over USB, or from one of its owners over the mesh.

Locked, the node answers nothing over Bluetooth but a hello, this phone included. Only USB, or one of its owners over the mesh, can unlock it. Lock a node you leave somewhere, once its owners are set.
Your node hasn\'t said how this one went. It keeps that only for messages since its firmware could, and may lose it when it restarts.
Straight from the other node: 1 hop
Signal strength of the last hop
A group message\'s writer hides how far off it is, so it may have come one hop less than this.
No message names the relays that passed it on. A trace does: Trace route, in the chat\'s menu.
The hops and signal are the acknowledgement\'s, on its way back. The other node sends it by its own route: most often through the same relays, but not always.
Hops, signal and round trip come once it\'s delivered, from the acknowledgement on its way back.
Update the node\'s firmware to trace
A trace goes out to %1$s the way your node\'s messages would, and comes back. Each node on the way adds itself, and how well it heard the one before.
Answered by %1$s, which keeps %2$s\'s messages while it sleeps: that\'s as far as they go until it wakes
Got as far as %1$s, which has no route to %2$s
No answer in time. %1$s may be out of reach, or a relay on the way may not pass traces on.
Handhelds (leaves) answer traces only from nodes they have a secure session with.
Not begun: your node has no route to %1$s
A trace shows the way frames went just then; the next message may go another way. Relays on the way can misreport it, and nothing checks what they add.
Tap a node with no name to give it one on this phone.
Only this phone shows the name. Nothing is sent, and a contact\'s name comes first.
Sends %1$s a numbered message every so often, and logs each: where this phone was, whether it was delivered and how. Keep this screen open while you move; the screen stays on.
No location: the log won\'t say where you were.
Not sent: the node refused it
This node\'s firmware says only whether each was delivered. Update it for hops, signal and round trip.
Its log goes when you leave. Export it first to keep it.
